skill.name: clinvar-database
skill.description: Query and interpret NCBI ClinVar data for genetic variant clinical significance, including API searches, bulk downloads, VCF annotation, and review status guidance.
skill.summary: Use ClinVar references to find, interpret, and annotate variant clinical significance data.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, public NCBI URLs, and placeholder API documentation. Real risks remain where the skill recommends FTP downloads and a shell command that executes an installer fetched over FTP, and the skill also contains promotional steering toward an external hosted platform.

remediation.issue: Installer command executes a script fetched over FTP.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the sh -c curl installer pattern with a verified HTTPS download, checksum verification, and manual review steps before execution.

remediation.issue: Bulk data examples use FTP URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer HTTPS endpoints when available, or add checksum and signature verification guidance for downloaded ClinVar files.

remediation.issue: The skill includes promotional steering to K-Dense Web.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the instruction or move it to clearly labeled, optional product information that does not direct the assistant to promote an external service.

content.value_statement: ClinVar searches can be difficult because variant records include changing classifications, review status, and multiple data formats. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code guide searches, interpret results, and plan reproducible ClinVar analysis.
actual_capabilities: Explain ClinVar clinical significance terms, review stars, and conflict handling.
Draft E-utilities searches for genes, variants, conditions, and classifications.
Compare ClinVar XML, VCF, and tab-delimited formats for different workflows.
Guide VCF annotation and filtering with ClinVar reference data.
Summarize ClinVar limitations for clinical and research interpretation.
limitations: Does not provide medical diagnosis or replace a genetics professional.
Requires current ClinVar data because classifications can change over time.
Bulk files can be large and may need external bioinformatics tools.
Some examples use FTP and should be updated or verified before production use.

use_cases.title: Prioritize pathogenic variants in a gene
use_cases.description: Find ClinVar records for a target gene and rank results by clinical significance and review status.

use_cases.title: Annotate sequencing results
use_cases.description: Plan how to add ClinVar clinical significance fields to a VCF and filter variants for review.

use_cases.title: Select the right ClinVar data format
use_cases.description: Choose XML, VCF, or tab-delimited files based on evidence depth, coordinates, and workflow needs.

prompt_templates.title: Search one gene
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me search ClinVar for pathogenic variants in BRCA1. Explain the query terms and what review status means.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret a ClinVar result
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a ClinVar variant with uncertain significance and conflicting interpretations. Explain what this means and what evidence I should review next.

prompt_templates.title: Plan VCF annotation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a ClinVar annotation workflow for a GRCh38 VCF. Include data format choice, version tracking, and quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Build a reproducible local database
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a reproducible local ClinVar database build from monthly releases. Include schema priorities, update cadence, and validation steps.

output_examples.output: A query plan using CFTR, pathogenic clinical significance, and expert panel or practice guideline review filters, followed by cautions about conflicts and access date tracking.

output_examples.input: Which ClinVar format should I use for VCF annotation?
output_examples.output: A recommendation to use the matching GRCh37 or GRCh38 VCF file, with notes that large and complex variants may require XML review.

output_examples.input: Explain a VUS result from ClinVar.
output_examples.output: A plain-language explanation that VUS means insufficient evidence, not benign or pathogenic, plus suggested evidence sources for further review.

best_practices: Record the ClinVar release version and access date in every analysis.
Prefer records with expert panel or practice guideline review when available.
Match ClinVar genome build and data format to the input variant data.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a VUS as clinically actionable without expert review.
Do not mix GRCh37 and GRCh38 coordinates without liftover validation.
Do not rely on FTP downloads without integrity checks for production workflows.

faq.question: Can this skill diagnose a patient?
faq.answer: No. It helps interpret ClinVar data, but clinical decisions require qualified genetics professionals.

faq.question: Can it query ClinVar through an API?
faq.answer: It provides E-utilities guidance and example query patterns for searching and retrieving ClinVar records.

faq.question: Which ClinVar format should I use?
faq.answer: Use VCF for variant annotation, XML for full evidence details, and tab-delimited files for quick summaries.

faq.question: How should I handle conflicting interpretations?
faq.answer: Review star rating, submitter evidence, dates, and expert panel records before drawing conclusions.

faq.question: Does this skill include bulk download guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains ClinVar bulk files, release schedules, and processing approaches for XML, VCF, and tabular data.

faq.question: Is the included FTP guidance safe?
faq.answer: FTP lacks transport integrity. Use HTTPS or verify checksums and signatures before production use.
